I need to answer this historical question about British monarchy succession.

Queen Anne ruled from 1702 to 1714. She was the last monarch of the House of Stuart. When she died in 1714 without surviving children, she was succeeded by George I of the House of Hanover, who was her second cousin.

George I became king because of the Act of Settlement 1701, which excluded Catholics from the throne and established that the crown would pass to Sophia of Hanover (a granddaughter of James I) and her Protestant descendants. Sophia died shortly before Anne, so her son George became king.

Answer: George I (George Louis of Hanover) succeeded Queen Anne to the throne in 1714.
